semantic_adjudication.reason: NL12 describes multiple independent conditions for activation: 'detecting pedestrians (pedestrian_detected), the rear distance being less than 5 meters with a velocity over 30 km/h (dist_to_rear<5 & vel>30), or the front distance being less than 15 meters in highway mode or 10 meters in urban mode.' PlantUML line 42 declares all these conditions as a single label: 'pedestrian_detected | (dist_to_rear<5 & vel>30) | (dist_to_front<15 in hwy mode or <10 in urban mode)'. In PlantUML semantics, a transition label is one trigger [guard] / effect; a pipe-separated list is not several triggers. The closed model therefore declares the entire text as a single opaque event, and none of the listed conditions can trigger the transition independently. This means the system cannot activate collision avoidance based on any single condition alone, contradicting NL12's description of independent triggering conditions. The model is internally consistent but diverges from the NL's intent.

decisions.reason: NL12 states 'The collision avoidance system is initially in the collision_avoidance_deactive state.' In UML hierarchical state machine semantics, 'initially in' is the normative meaning of an initial pseudostate edge. The complete FCSTM transition inventory for scope CollisionAvoidanceSystem contains only three transitions: line:71 ([*] -> UnspecifiedInitial, compiler-synthetic), line:72 (deactive -> active), line:73 (active -> deactive). No author-authored initial entry to collision_avoidance_deactive exists. The source PlantUML (lines 41-43) independently confirms the absence: no [*] arrow to collision_avoidance_deactive appears within the CollisionAvoidanceSystem block. Predicate S2 (transition_exists) returned verdict=false for the expected edge. The only alternative reading ('logical default state rather than explicit UML initial edge') is defeated because UML semantics define initial pseudostate edges as the exclusive mechanism for declaring a default entry state in a composite.
decisions.violated_obligation: CollisionAvoidanceSystem's initial pseudostate edge must target collision_avoidance_deactive, establishing it as the default entry state of the composite.

decisions.basis: NL1 requirement quote; FCSTM transition line 75 with triggers=[Autonomous_mode_start]; verify fact initial-entry:transition:line:75 status=refuted with has_trigger=true; inspection diagnostic INITIAL_ENTRY_CONDITIONAL on line 75.
decisions.reason: NL1 states 'The system begins in the AutonomousMode state, which transitions into the InitialState substate, marking the starting point of the autonomous driving mode.' The FCSTM root initial entry transition (line 75: [*] -> AutonomousMode) carries the trigger Autonomous_mode_start, making it conditional. issues.reason: The NL states the system 'begins in the AutonomousMode state,' which in state-machine semantics implies an unconditional initial entry. The FCSTM makes this entry conditional on an external event. The deterministic verify fact refutes the initial-entry property. The behavioral consequence is that the entire AutonomousMode subsystem (and all driving behavior) is inert until an external trigger fires, contradicting the NL's description of AutonomousMode as the starting point.
issues.requirement_quote: The system begins in the AutonomousMode state, which transitions into the InitialState substate, marking the starting point of the autonomous driving mode.
issues.strongest_rebuttal: The PlantUML source explicitly labels the initial transition 'Autonomous mode start,' which the compiler faithfully lowered as a trigger. One could argue the author intended a triggered start rather than an unconditional one, and the NL word 'begins' is ambiguous between 'starts automatically' and 'can start upon a signal.'
issues.title: Root initial entry to AutonomousMode is conditional on Autonomous_mode_start event

issues.basis: NL1 text; FCSTM transition line 63 ([*] -> InitialState in scope AutonomousMode, triggers=[Start_of_autonomous_driving_mode]); verify fact initial-entry:transition:line:63 status=refuted details has_trigger=true; inspection diagnostic INITIAL_ENTRY_CONDITIONAL line 63; contract REF-002 owner=AutonomousMode target=InitialState.
issues.expected: Within AutonomousMode, the initial entry to InitialState is unconditional, so the system automatically enters InitialState upon entering AutonomousMode.
issues.observed: The FCSTM AutonomousMode initial entry transition (line 63: [*] -> InitialState) carries the trigger Start_of_autonomous_driving_mode, making it conditional. The deterministic verify fact refutes this as a proper initial entry (has_trigger=true). Even after entering AutonomousMode, the system does not automatically reach InitialState.
issues.reason: The NL describes the system as transitioning 'into the InitialState substate, marking the starting point of the autonomous driving mode.' This implies InitialState is the automatic first state within AutonomousMode. The FCSTM gates this entry behind an external event. The behavioral consequence is that even after resolving the root entry issue, the system would not automatically reach the operational starting point (InitialState) without a second external trigger.
issues.requirement_quote: The system begins in the AutonomousMode state, which transitions into the InitialState substate, marking the starting point of the autonomous driving mode.
issues.strongest_rebuttal: The PlantUML source explicitly labels this transition 'Start of autonomous driving mode,' suggesting the author intended a two-phase start (first enter AutonomousMode, then activate the driving mode). The NL phrase 'transitions into' could be read as describing a triggered transition rather than an automatic initial entry.
issues.title: AutonomousMode initial entry to InitialState is conditional on Start_of_autonomous_driving_mode event

issues.basis: NL12 text; FCSTM transition inventory: no transition targets CollisionAvoidanceSystem from root or any reachable state; verify facts: reachability:state:CollisionAvoidanceSystem:line:67 refuted, reachability:state:collision_avoidance_deactive:line:68 refuted, reachability:state:collision_avoidance_active:line:69 refuted, reachability:state:UnspecifiedInitial:line:70 refuted; inspection facts: STATE_UNREACHABLE_FROM_INITIAL for lines 67-70; reachable_state_count=15, unreachable_state_count=4.
issues.expected: The CollisionAvoidanceSystem composite is reachable from the root initial entry, allowing the system to activate its collision avoidance behavior.
issues.observed: The FCSTM has no transition from root or any reachable state to CollisionAvoidanceSystem. The deterministic verify fact refutes reachability for CollisionAvoidanceSystem (state:line:67) and all its children (collision_avoidance_deactive:line:68, collision_avoidance_active:line:69, UnspecifiedInitial:line:70). The reachable set from initial contains 15 states, none in the CollisionAvoidanceSystem subtree.
issues.reason: NL12 describes the collision avoidance system as an operational component that is 'initially in' a state and responds to events. For this behavior to be activatable in the closed model, the composite must be reachable from the root initial entry. The complete FCSTM transition inventory shows no edge from any reachable state to CollisionAvoidanceSystem. The verify facts confirm refuted reachability for the composite and all descendants. The behavioral consequence is that the entire collision avoidance subsystem is dead code in the closed model: no event can trigger any of its transitions.
issues.requirement_quote: The collision avoidance system is initially in the collision_avoidance_deactive state. It transitions to collision_avoidance_active when certain conditions are met, such as detecting pedestrians (`pedestrian_detected`), the rear distance being less than 5 meters with a velocity over 30 km/h (`dist_to_rear<5 & vel>30`), or the front distance being less than 15 meters in highway mode or 10 meters in urban mode.
issues.strongest_rebuttal: CollisionAvoidanceSystem could be intended as an independent, externally-triggered subsystem that operates in parallel with AutonomousMode rather than as a child of the main driving state machine. The NL describes it in separate paragraphs (NL12-13) from the autonomous driving mode (NL1-11), which might suggest orthogonal operation. However, the FCSTM places it under the same root, and no entry mechanism is provided.
issues.title: CollisionAvoidanceSystem is unreachable from the system root initial entry

issues.basis: NL12 (activation event response) and NL13 (deactivation event response); FCSTM event_consumer facts: pedestrian_detected... consumer_transition_refs=[transition:line:72] reachable_consumer_transition_refs=[]; front_inactive... consumer_transition_refs=[transition:line:73] reachable_consumer_transition_refs=[]; verify facts: event-consumer:pedestrian_detected... refuted, event-consumer:front_inactive... refuted; inspection diagnostics: EVENT_CONSUMER_UNREACHABLE for both events.
issues.expected: The collision avoidance activation and deactivation events have at least one reachable consumer transition in the CollisionAvoidanceSystem scope, so that the NL-described event response can be triggered during operation.
issues.observed: Both events have declared consumer transitions (line 72 for activation, line 73 for deactivation) but the deterministic verify facts refute reachable consumer coverage for both: reachable_consumer_transition_refs are empty for each. The inspection diagnostics confirm EVENT_CONSUMER_UNREACHABLE for both events. The consumers are unreachable because the enclosing composite CollisionAvoidanceSystem is itself unreachable from root.
issues.reason: NL12 and NL13 establish that the collision avoidance system must respond to danger detection events (activating) and danger inactivation events (deactivating). In the closed model, both events have consumer transitions declared but none is reachable. Declaration-only presence cannot discharge operational coverage: in the current model, firing either event produces no state change. This is a distinct property from the composite reachability (which is about whether the scope can be entered) and the initial_entry (which is about the correct first state within the scope). Even if reachability were fixed, a separate defect in the initial entry (wrong target) would still prevent the system from reaching the deactive state where the activation event is consumed.
issues.requirement_quote: The collision avoidance system is initially in the collision_avoidance_deactive state. It transitions to collision_avoidance_active when certain conditions are met, such as detecting pedestrians (`pedestrian_detected`), the rear distance being less than 5 meters with a velocity over 30 km/h (`dist_to_rear<5 & vel>30`), or the front distance being less than 15 meters in highway mode or 10 meters in urban mode.
issues.strongest_rebuttal: The consumer transitions exist and are correctly declared within the CollisionAvoidanceSystem scope. If the composite were made reachable (fixing the root reachability issue), the consumers would become reachable and the events would be properly covered. The event_consumer_coverage failure is entirely caused by the upstream reachability defect and may be considered a derivative rather than an independent obligation.
issues.title: Collision avoidance events have declared consumers but no reachable consumer transitions

semantic_adjudication.basis: NL12 requirement quote listing multiple independent conditions; PlantUML line 42 raw label showing all conditions in one label; FCSTM event identity confirming single opaque event; candidate basis identifying exact transition and event references.
semantic_adjudication.reason: NL12 describes multiple independent conditions for activation: 'detecting pedestrians (pedestrian_detected), the rear distance being less than 5 meters with a velocity over 30 km/h (dist_to_rear<5 & vel>30), or the front distance being less than 15 meters in highway mode or 10 meters in urban mode.' PlantUML line 42 declares all these conditions as a single label: 'pedestrian_detected | (dist_to_rear<5 & vel>30) | (dist_to_front<15 in hwy mode or <10 in urban mode)'. In PlantUML semantics, a transition label is one trigger [guard] / effect; a pipe-separated list is not several triggers. The closed model therefore declares the entire text as a single opaque event, and none of the listed conditions can trigger the transition independently. This means the system cannot activate collision avoidance based on any single condition alone, contradicting NL12's description of independent triggering conditions. The model is internally consistent but diverges from the NL's intent.
semantic_adjudication.violated_obligation: Each condition that may trigger the collision_avoidance_deactive to collision_avoidance_active transition must be a separately triggerable event or guard, as NL12 describes multiple independent activation conditions.

decisions.reason: NL12 states 'The collision avoidance system is initially in the collision_avoidance_deactive state.' In UML hierarchical state machine semantics, 'initially in' is the normative meaning of an initial pseudostate edge. The complete FCSTM transition inventory for scope CollisionAvoidanceSystem contains only three transitions: line:71 ([*] -> UnspecifiedInitial, compiler-synthetic), line:72 (deactive -> active), line:73 (active -> deactive). No author-authored initial entry to collision_avoidance_deactive exists. The source PlantUML (lines 41-43) independently confirms the absence: no [*] arrow to collision_avoidance_deactive appears within the CollisionAvoidanceSystem block. Predicate S2 (transition_exists) returned verdict=false for the expected edge. The only alternative reading ('logical default state rather than explicit UML initial edge') is defeated because UML semantics define initial pseudostate edges as the exclusive mechanism for declaring a default entry state in a composite.

decisions.basis: NL1 requirement quote; FCSTM transition line 75 with triggers=[Autonomous_mode_start]; verify fact initial-entry:transition:line:75 status=refuted with has_trigger=true; inspection diagnostic INITIAL_ENTRY_CONDITIONAL on line 75.
decisions.reason: NL1 states 'The system begins in the AutonomousMode state, which transitions into the InitialState substate, marking the starting point of the autonomous driving mode.' The FCSTM root initial entry transition (line 75: [*] -> AutonomousMode) carries the trigger Autonomous_mode_start, making it conditional. In UML, an initial pseudostate edge must be unconditional; a trigger on an initial transition violates this language invariant. candidate.observed: Both events have declared consumer transitions (line 72 for activation, line 73 for deactivation) but the deterministic verify facts refute reachable consumer coverage for both: reachable_consumer_transition_refs are empty for each. The inspection diagnostics confirm EVENT_CONSUMER_UNREACHABLE for both events. The consumers are unreachable because the enclosing composite CollisionAvoidanceSystem is itself unreachable from root.
candidate.reason: NL12 and NL13 establish that the collision avoidance system must respond to danger detection events (activating) and danger inactivation events (deactivating). Declaration-only presence cannot discharge operational coverage: in the current model, firing either event produces no state change. This is a distinct property from the composite reachability (which is about whether the scope can be entered) and the initial_entry (which is about the correct first state within the scope). Even if reachability were fixed, a separate defect in the initial entry (wrong target) would still prevent the system from reaching the deactive state where the activation event is consumed.

If the composite were made reachable (fixing the root reachability issue), the consumers would become reachable and the events would be properly covered. The event_consumer_coverage failure is entirely caused by the upstream reachability defect and may be considered a derivative rather than an independent obligation.
